q: Is this normal for a 3 year old? I’m not sure how to handle this when it happens aside from comforting him and leaving.
cx: Shy just-3-year-old panicked at a community pool locker room and begged to go home.

q: We have tried every kind of parenting style and appropriate discipline for her age and NOTHING IS WORKING. I am completely worn down and I am looking for any suggestion we are struggling so badly.
cx: 3-year-old who hits and bites the whole family; bedtimes take hours.

q: My mom has told me that I need to “fix this” and “you have a problem here” when it comes to her current behavior.
cx: Mother two weeks after a C-section; her 4-year-old regressed as expected; the grandmother is staying with them.

q: My mom is irritating me more than my daughter.
cx: Same mother.

q: I have been doing my best to give her 10-15 minutes of time with only me, which some days she really doesn’t want to do that.
cx: Same mother; one-on-one time offered and sometimes refused.

q: I think my mom disrupted a lot, especially how I handle things. I think my mom probably told her not to touch things first and I’m sure I felt that I had to do the same thing.
cx: Same mother, after a reply; she had moved to 'pick your battles'.

q: This is actually very reassuring to me. I’ve been really needing a modern perspective. Thank you!
cx: Same mother, set against her mother's view.

q: Have tried asking daycare to use the toilets on the other floors (they are 2F in a 3 story, 1F and 3F both have normal toilets) but they seem resistant, not the least of which is because of the distance to go there.
cx: Just-3-year-old who will only use adult-size toilets; daycare has only small ones on his floor.

q: I'm working with daycare on this, they sometimes are putting one on them and I'm explaining to not do this
cx: The daycare puts a diaper on the child against the parent's plan.

q: What's worse, the next day they were a nightmare at daycare, doing things they never do. Throwing toys at other kids, flipping tables, truly lucky we didn't just get kicked out I think.
cx: After one attempt at waking the child for a night pee.

q: Getting discouraged because I have no idea how to address any issue, and especially with daycare it just feels like nothing will ever change.
cx: Same parent closing the post.

q: I even got him a watch that buzzes every hour to remind him to use the potty. That lasted about a month and worked well but then he started taking it off and it got lost.
cx: 4-year-old with near-daily accidents since daycare at 3; kindergarten soon.

q: I get I probably messed up somewhere down the line but everyone I speak to doesn’t have any good advice.
cx: Same parent.

q: From what the daycare people tell me, he is distracted playing and doesn’t want to stop which leads to him peeing himself.
cx: The daycare's explanation.

q: And my tolerance of my son’s neediness and tantrums just make me lose it.
cx: Mother of a 2-year-old whose rage tracks her insomnia; newly pregnant again.

q: I’m 2 years postpartum and have just been starting to feel like myself again, so the thought of another couple years of struggling through another newborn to toddler experience just has me feeling scared and worried
cx: Same mother.

q: Is the best approach those intensive weekends? Or is there a lower pressure version that still gets the job done?
cx: Mother 7 months pregnant with a 25-month-old in low-pressure sitting; a nanny helps.

q: I don’t want to push him. I want to do what’s right for him and his body, but I want to make sure I’m also giving him the confidence that he needs.
cx: Mother of a very verbal 2.5-year-old who does not mind wet diapers.

q: And yes, I was just waiting for some kind of huge sign like oh hey I’m totally ready to learn this. Otherwise, I’ve just been doing a little small doses because I don’t want to do something wrong and have it be negative.
cx: Same mother, after replies about readiness.

q: Oh gosh a lot. Some from his pediatrician, friends etc.
cx: Asked how much advice she has already had.

q: As a former daycare teacher and nanny who has potty trained so many kids. I have literally tried everything and nothing works. She doesn’t care at all.
cx: Two years of an almost-4-year-old not pooping on the potty.

q: We start full time preschool in August and they expect her to be 100% trained.
cx: Same parent; the preschool rule as the deadline.

q: I have no idea what else to try at this point. I’m about to just go back to buying diapers and canceling going back to school.
cx: Same parent.

q: She fluctuates between 10-15 percentile and has always been a small girl so I am not really on board with the whole "I provide the food she chooses to eat it" method because I am so worried about her losing weight she doesn't have to lose.
cx: Pregnant stay-at-home mother of an almost-2.5-year-old who now eats mostly dairy and carbs.

q: I'm a SAHM so this is all on me throughout the day and it's just been draining. I feel like the majority of our day if me fighting her to eat or sleep.
cx: Same mother.

q: It is really heartbreaking to watch him cry like he was devastated.
cx: Mother of a 22-month-old in his first week of hour-long daycare sessions.

q: His reaction really makes me think if this is necessary.
cx: Same mother; daycare is optional for them.
